thread.title: In March of 2015 I purchased 15 of the largest cap Dividend

author: Dale Roberts
title: In March of 2015 I purchased 15 of the largest cap Dividend
text:
In March of 2015 I purchased 15 of the largest cap Dividend Achievers ( VIG ). I did no additional financial evaluation other than reading that list. The 15 companies that I added are 3M (NYSE: MMM ), Pepsi (NYSE: PEP ), CVS Health Corporation (NYSE: CVS ), Wal-Mart (NYSE: WMT ), Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ ), Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM ), United Technologies (NYSE: UTX ), Lowe's (NYSE: LOW ), Walgreens Boots Alliance (NASDAQ: WBA ), Medtronic (NYSE: MDT ), Nike (NYSE: NKE ), Abbott Labs (NYSE: ABT ), Colgate-Palmolive (NYSE: CL ), Texas Instruments (NYSE: TXN ) and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ).
And the returns of those 15 Achievers have danced around the total return line for the total index ETF VIG offered by Vanguard. Here are the 15 Achievers as Portfolio 1 vs the ETF courtesy of portfoliovisualizer.com. Of course past performance does not guarantee future returns. The period is March of 2015 to end of December 2017.
I initially had planned to hold 20-25 Achievers even though 15 appears to 'be enough'. But I also hold 3 'picks' by way of Apple ( AAPL ), BlackRock ( BLK ) and Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK.B ) and given those additions and the potential added diversification of these 3 S&P 500 ( IVV ) members, I stopped at 15 Achievers plus 3 picks. Apple and BlackRock are longer term growth picks and they are doing their job. Here's my article My 2 Long Term Growth Picks Beat The Market By 22% in 2017 . I know that's an embarrassment for an indexer and index skimmer. BRK.B is held in the hope that Mr. Buffett can do what he does best - beat the market through a major market correction. You might have noticed that we have not had one of those corrections in a few years. But enough about this indexer's stock picking luck.
